text: Bitcoin has lost almost half its value since its record a year ago.
Some people lost everything. Others didn't even blink.
In the river town, everyone wants the new golden fish. And every week, its price goes up.
The first man wants to get rich fast. So he borrows twenty baskets of fish, and buys golden fish at the top.
The second man thinks it's a silly fish. He buys none.
The third man buys just one. With fish he can afford to lose. And he borrows nothing.
Then, one morning, the price falls by half.
The second man laughs. The third man shrugs, and waits.
But the first man's lender is at the door. Pay me back. Today.
His golden fish are worth half. So he sells every single one, at the bottom, to the third man.
Maybe the price comes back. Maybe it doesn't. The first man will never find out.
The crash didn't ruin him. The loan did.
On November thirteenth, one point six billion dollars of borrowed crypto bets were force-sold in a single day.
Prices fall for everyone. Only borrowed money makes you sell at the bottom.
